Network inventory

Review a completed Nmap report as host and port-state counts. These observations are separate from traffic and detection severity; an open port is not a confirmed threat.

No inventory loaded. Files stay in this tab.

Hosts reported by Nmap

Protocols · individually listed ports

Individually listed port states

Grouped port states

Counts describe the selected report, not current reachability or complete network coverage. Grouped ports have no protocol breakdown in this summary. Source authenticity is unverified.

Prepare an inventory summary

With the updated MEGALODON package installed, run this in its Python environment against an existing completed report. No Nmap installation or scan is required. On Linux, set private output permissions first.

umask 077
python -m megalodon.nmap_inventory < completed-report.xml > inventory-summary.json

Then load inventory-summary.json above. The supported profile is Nmap 7.x, XML 1.05, completed successfully, at most 2 MiB and 4,096 represented hosts. Addresses, names, port numbers, banners, scripts and command arguments are omitted. Failed or timed-out reports are refused. No data is uploaded or saved by this page.

Completed file scan

Review counts from a completed ClamAV clamscan report. This is separate from network traffic and its danger levels.

No scan summary loaded. Files stay in this tab.

Counts come from the selected report; the source is not authenticated. Zero detections do not prove complete coverage or that the files are safe. No scan runs or updates automatically.

Prepare a scan summary

After an operator-run clamscan finishes, retain its output and exit status privately. Run this command with the matching exit status (0 for no matches, 1 for matches); exit status 2 and reported errors are refused. The report may include private paths, so only load the exported JSON into the HUD.

umask 077
python -m megalodon.clamav_summary --exit-code 0 < completed-clamscan.txt > scan-summary.json

Replace 0 with the recorded exit status when it is 1. The exporter reads at most 1 MiB; it emits only times, version and counts. Times printed by clamscan are local and have no timezone. This page holds the aggregate only until cleared or closed.

Saved package inventory

Review one completed osquery package count. This is host inventory, separate from network traffic and findings.

No package count loaded.

Saved, unauthenticated result. This count does not establish package safety, update status or live osquery health. Files remain in this tab.

Prepare a package count

On a trusted Ubuntu PC with osquery already installed, run the fixed read-only query yourself. Inspect the saved result, then export and load only the counts-only JSON. Do not put package names, paths or arbitrary query output into the HUD.

umask 077
osqueryi --json 'SELECT count(*) AS package_count FROM deb_packages;' > private-osquery-result.json
python -m megalodon.osquery_inventory < private-osquery-result.json > package-count.json

A successful command alone does not authenticate the saved file or prove complete host inventory. The exporter refuses unexpected fields and inputs over 4 KiB.

Offline / inert

  • No TAXII, persistence, model, attribution, or action

Trust membrane

Autonomy stops before authority.

Detections support review; they do not prove malicious activity. Model advice is untrusted commentary, never evidence or permission to change a host.

Security review ↗
01

Metadata only

No packet payloads or payload-derived hashes enter the core event model.

02

Loopback by default

Core telemetry reads stay on 127.0.0.1:8787. A separate, disabled-by-default AI question POST requires an operator token and writes private AI receipts. This hosted Site cannot call either local route.

03

Local core operation

The local core requires no cloud account. This hosted Site uses hosting/sign-in services; external setup links leave the Site.

04

Plan, do not apply

Firewall proposals are inert. Live application remains explicitly refused.

05

Bounded local AI

The optional client allows one bounded loopback request with no action authority. The separately operated model process is not confined by those client checks.

06

Finite evidence

Implemented operations have documented bounds. The Suricata 512 MiB logical store ceiling is not a whole-disk or retention budget; retention remains operator-owned.

Where the bytes live

Tracked source vs. runtime-only storage

Quoted from docs/storage-layout.md ↗. Cloning this repository creates only the left lane; the right lane exists only after an operator runs the named command.

Tracked in git

  • config/*.tomlTyped defaults and the fixed detection-rule reference
  • contracts/*/v1/Inert schemas and accepted/rejected fixtures
  • megalodon/reference/*Pinned IANA snapshot and synthetic evaluation corpus
  • site/dist/This static console mirror; no process reads it at runtime
run a command →

Runtime-only, gitignored

  • data/megalodon.dbAudit ledger; 256 MiB default high-water stop
  • captures/, logs/Operator-authorized adapter input, never created automatically
  • offline-runs/One mode-0700 report-set directory per analysis run
  • --suricata-db <path>Operator-selected store; 512 MiB logical ceiling

No command shares one path across stores. Each keeps its own owner-private directory and mode checks, so one store's failure or migration cannot touch another's.
